rationale: PACKAGE ANNOTATION (JLS 7.4.1: annotations on a package declaration, the package-info.java shape). An annotation is a type mention and must emit `references` from the annotated declaration. The package is the ONE annotated declaration that publishes no symbol, so the source is the package NAME (the identity its `exports` rows use) and `annotatedKind` is `package_declaration`. The source cannot come from `currentPackage`: the annotation is written BEFORE the package declaration and the single-pass walk visits it first, so pre-fix this file emitted ZERO relationships (probe: 0 symbols, 0 relationships). The file-level annotation fallback therefore finds the package name in the tree instead of from walk state. Authored from Java semantics before the fix; the forbid pins that no fabricated source (`global`/`root`) is used, because an edge whose source names nothing is worse than a missing one.

forbidRelationships.comment: the package name is the annotated declaration's identity; `global` is the no-scope fallback and names nothing here
same rule; `root` is the file-level import fallback, not a package
